biography.plain_text: Nimet Arif Kurtel is a Turkish coal-mining businessman and racehorse breeder who founded İmbat Madencilik. His equestrian interests grew from visits to Istanbul's racecourse and later leadership of the İzmir Equestrian Club. He owns Kurtel Stud in Urla, and his horse Long Runner twice won Turkey's Presidential Cup in successive years.

long_biography.plain_text:
Racehorse breeder Nimet Arif Kurtel chose to keep a valuable yearling rather than sell it at Keeneland in 2017. The colt was a full brother to champion Shared Belief, and Kurtel wanted to race him in the United States. He had bought their mother, Common Hope, while she was carrying another foal, then developed the family through matings in Turkey and America.

Managing horses across countries required regular contact with the people caring for them. Kurtel set aside the early morning, between five and seven, to speak with his horse managers before turning to his mining work. His breeding programme focused on producing runners for his own stable, with young horses prepared by specialist trainers before their racing careers.
